ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A small square with side length $4 \mathrm{~cm}$ is drawn within a big square with side length $10 \mathrm{~cm}$; their sides are parallel to each other (see diagram). What percentage of the figure is shaded?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a large square containing a smaller square whose sides are parallel to the large square. The shaded parts are exactly the top trapezoid and the bottom trapezoid between the two squares; the left and right regions are unshaded. Each shaded trapezoid has one horizontal base along the large square of length 10 cm and the other horizontal base along the small square of length 4 cm. Reasoning: Let the vertical heights of the top and bottom shaded trapezoids be h1 and h2. Since the large square has total height 10 cm and the small square has height 4 cm, the remaining vertical distance split between the top and bottom trapezoids is h1 + h2 = 10 - 4 = 6 cm. The combined shaded area is the sum of the two trapezoid areas: ((10 + 4)/2)h1 + ((10 + 4)/2)h2 = ((10 + 4)/2)(h1 + h2) = 7 × 6 = 42 square cm. The area of the large square is 10^2 = 100 square cm. Therefore, the shaded percentage is 42/100 = 42%.

method.method_draft: Compute the unshaded area first and subtract from the big square. From the image, the unshaded portions are the central small square plus the left and right side trapezoids. From the text, the outer square side is 10 cm and the inner square side is 4 cm. The central unshaded square has area 4^2 = 16. For the left and right unshaded trapezoids, the parallel vertical bases are 10 and 4; if their horizontal widths are w1 and w2, then w1 + w2 = 10 - 4 = 6.
